pages.text: "Grandma, look at me!" Yuki bounced in the room. Grandma looked only into a box beside the brazier. A baby bird she had found in the yard that morning lay inside. "Shh, you'll startle it." Yuki's cheeks puffed sulkily.
"In front of the brazier is my place!" Yuki pushed the box into a corner and sat in the warmest spot.
But Grandma moved the box back beside the brazier. Yuki pulled the quilt over their head and turned away. "There's no place for me now..." Yuki gripped the quilt tighter.
Grandma lifted the quilt. "You're much bigger than that baby. Big children have things they can give." She held Yuki's hand tightly.
Yuki came out and peered into the box. Thin peeps sounded. The fluffy baby bird shivered. "Oh... is it still cold?"
Yuki pushed the box into the warmest spot beside the brazier. The shivering slowly stopped, and the peeps grew fuller. "I'm Bigger, So I'll Share!"
Yuki pulled a cushion beside the box, making a place of their own. "Here's my new place!" Grandma smiled. Yuki's sulky feeling had settled away.
Now Yuki knew just by listening: thin peeps meant cold; fuller peeps meant fine. Brown dog Momo lay with their nose beside the box, too.
As soon as Yuki woke, they wrapped and tied the scarf. "One, share the warm spot! Two, look when I hear a sound! Three, speak gently!" Yuki went to the box first.
Grandma hugged Yuki. "You're a big child now." When someone little arrived, Yuki had things to give. Smiling into the box, Yuki said, "I'm Bigger, So I'll Share!"
